verdict.rationale: Raygun documents deployment tracking to surface new errors and regressions, a Deployments API, per-error version data with version filters, and native GitHub/Bitbucket/GitLab repo integrations. Nothing in the evidence shows an issue displaying the release it first appeared in, or Raygun identifying a suspect commit. missing for 10: documented first-seen-release attribution on issues, suspect-commit identification, commit-to-error association details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can associate errors with releases and commits so each issue shows the release it first appeared in and the suspect commit that likely caused it

citations.quote: Track every deployment in real time to identify any new errors or regressions.
You'll need your external access token for the following services: Deployments API
use smart filters to segment errors by date, location, version, host, OS, browser, and custom tags
Connect to your repo through native integrations with GitHub, Bitbucket, and GitLab
